top.title: Barcelona see €70 million summer signing as ‘the new Raphinha’ after impressive start
top.description: Barcelona see €70 million summer signing as ‘the new Raphinha’ after impressive start Barcelona are comparing Anthony Gordon to Raphinha because of his work rate and defensive contribution, according to Mundo Deportivo . The report states that the England international has settled quickly into Hansi Flick’s squad and has impressed not only with his numbers, but also with the way he approaches the matches. On that note, Gordon’s pressing, running and willingness to track back are considered valuable in Barcelona’s structure, where forwards must contribute without the ball. Gordon has found his place in Barcelona’s dressing room The outlet mentions that Gordon, who signed for Barcelona for €70 million past summer, has built strong relationships with the likes of Eric Garcia, Dani Olmo and Pedri, who have helped him adapt to life at the club. Garcia and Olmo speak English well and have been important points of support, while Pedri has also helped him connect with the group. Anthony Gordon has impressed everyone at Barcelona. (Picture credit: Barcelona website) His integration matters because Flick’s system depends on coordinated movement and trust. Moreover, Gordon sees Barcelona as a project where he can compete for titles, establish himself among Europe’s elite and strengthen his standing internationally. Work rate is central to the Raphinha comparison Gordon is a skilful and powerful winger who combines attacking ability with a high level of physical effort. He presses opponents, tracks back and continues running throughout matches. These qualities have drawn comparisons with Raphinha, whose commitment without possession has become a defining part of his game at Barcelona. Anthony Gordon is called ‘ a second Raphinha ‘. (Picture credit: X/@FCBarcelona) In fact, those within the club call him “a second Raphinha” thanks to his similarities with the Brazilian style, where his defensive efforts help the team maintain its intensity. Decision-making is an area to improve Despite his promising start, Gordon recognises that he still has room to develop. One of his priorities is improving his decision-making, particularly identifying when to take on an opponent and when to choose a pass or another option. For what it is worth, his experience in English football has largely been influenced by a more direct, box-to-box style, but at Barcelona, he is learning to operate within a possession-based system that requires careful reading of space and movement.

top.title: Real Madrid midfield star rediscovers his best form under Jose Mourinho
top.description: Real Madrid midfield star rediscovers his best form under Jose Mourinho Real Madrid have enjoyed an excellent resurgence under Jose Mourinho over the past couple of months. Several individual performances have been crucial for Los Blancos , but none has been more striking than Jude Bellingham’s return to his devastating best. After a couple of difficult seasons in the Spanish capital, Bellingham is back to the form that took Spanish football by storm during his debut season at the club. Having a fully fit and firing Bellingham is great news for Los Blancos, especially with Madrid aspiring to win trophies this season. Arsenal legend Thierry Henry has praised Bellingham’s form and has identified Real Madrid as title contenders this campaign. “Real Madrid put in a great performance; playing like that, they’re contenders for the Champions League. “They’re improving a lot as the weeks go by. Something’s happening at Real Madrid – watch out,” he explained. His influence on the team is now beginning to extend beyond just his ability to score goals and provide assists. Bellingham rediscovering his match-winning instincts The midweek clash against PSV Eindhoven provided the perfect demonstration of what Bellingham can add to this team. Bellingham has returned to his very best this season. (Photo by Tullio M. Puglia/Getty Images) The Englishman came on at half-time with Los Blancos struggling to impose themselves and trailing 1-0. He immediately turned the game on its head, scoring a spectacular goal that will be remembered for a long time. Bellingham has already scored seven goals this season, just one fewer than he managed throughout last season. The numbers are moving closer to the kind of attacking output he produced in his debut season in the Spanish capital. Bellingham scored 23 goals and provided 13 assists from midfield to help Los Blancos complete the La Liga and Champions League double. Mourinho has unlocked a different Bellingham Under Jose Mourinho, Bellingham has combined his attacking instincts with greater defensive discipline. He has always been an intelligent presser, but the Englishman is also taking more responsibility in possession and influencing play. The best example of this came in the Clasico that Real Madrid won back in October. With the game heading for a draw, Bellingham helped his team secure all three points. Bellingham is evolving into a complete midfielder under Jose Mourinho. top.title: How Fury and Joshua changed British boxing forever
top.description: Tyson Fury (left) has 36 wins, two defeats and one draw as a professional, while Anthony Joshua has 30 wins and four defeats [Getty Images] They have conquered the world, filled stadiums and transformed British boxing. Now, after more than a decade of lingering tension and endless debate, Tyson Fury and Anthony Joshua are finally preparing to share a ring. They are from different worlds, with contrasting personalities and wildly different journeys to the summit of heavyweight boxing. Fury is the unpredictable showman who dethroned a seemingly unbeatable champion. Joshua is the Olympic golden boy who became a global superstar. Who is better? Who has achieved more? The arguments have raged in pubs, boxing gyms and across social media. We may soon get our answer, but whatever happens when the first bell sounds in Cardiff in the early hours of 12 December, their greatest achievement may already be secure. Together, Joshua and Fury have taken British heavyweight boxing to new heights, attracting wider audiences and inspiring the next generation. How Fury and Joshua brought big-time heavyweight boxing to Britain Britain had produced heavyweight champions before, but for years many of the division's biggest fights took place overseas. Lennox Lewis fought some of his defining bouts in Las Vegas and Memphis. Challengers travelled to Germany when the Klitschko brothers reigned. In November 2015, Fury outpointed Wladimir Klitschko in Dusseldorf. Less than five months later, Joshua knocked out Charles Martin at London's O2 Arena to win his first world title in his 16th professional fight. "Bosh, that's it. The revolution starts in that six-month period," said BBC Radio 5 Live boxing pundit Steve Bunce, who was interviewed for the BBC documentary Rivals: Fury v Joshua. Joshua's former trainer Rob McCracken saw an early sign of his appeal in Birmingham, where a show sold out with Joshua on the undercard. "I'm from Birmingham, and it's hard to get a big crowd that sort of size," McCracken says. Promoters soon realised Joshua was bringing in a different audience and could sell tickets almost instantly. By 2017, Joshua was fighting in front of 90,000 fans at Wembley Stadium, where he stopped Klitschko, while Fury's trilogy with Deontay Wilder made him a box-office draw in the USA. "The two of them have been in eight massive stadium fights over an eight-year period," Bunce says. "That's reshaping British boxing history." Yet for all the domestic ground they broke, both men eventually helped export the division's biggest nights back overseas - trading British stadiums for Saudi Arabian paydays, with even this Cardiff homecoming bankrolled by Turki Alalshikh's 'Riyadh Season' and timed for an American streaming audience. top.title: What makes or breaks a high press?
top.description: Alexander Isak and Florian Wirtz spearhead Liverpool's press under Andoni Iraola [Getty Images] A good high press has been the basis for some of the most successful sides in modern football but a well-oiled pressing machine has many moving parts - all requiring close attention. When an out-of-possession plan is implemented poorly, entire seasons can fall apart. So, what determines whether a press works or fails? And how are the always-adapting Premier League teams exploiting high presses this season? 1. Establishing intent When a team decides to press, they must first establish their intention. This informs how the players act. Speaking to DAZN Portugal , Brighton manager Fabian Hurzeler was asked about whether a good press relied more on physicality or courage. "A really good question," he began. "When you want to press high you need the courage and mindset to do it. Our mindset is we press to score, we don't just press to win the ball back." In coaching, clarity is key - particularly when it comes to creating alignment in the squad and Hurzeler is deliberate in simplifying big ideas when delivering messages to his players, a skill he practised as a radio pundit during the World Cup. "[Punditry] helps you as a coach in that you have to summarise things in a short and easy way so that everyone understands," he said. "Football might get more complex but simplicity counts." Hurzeler's "pressing to score" is a phrase that communicates many ideas in a memorable three words: intensity, being proactive, and immediate forward-thinking on winning the ball. It also frames pressing in a way that makes it easy for attackers to buy into, in the form of goals. "You want commitment from everyone on the pitch," Hurzeler explained. "If just one has doubts, the whole press is gone." The Red Bull school of coaching uses a similarly succinct phrase - "the last step" to address these ideas around intention, collectiveness and aggression. Summarised by Tactx , whose coaches have worked under the Red Bull model, the last step refers to "players [being] coached to attack through the opponent, using the final step to lunge aggressively at the ball". "This action commits the defender fully and is often the decisive moment that allows possession to be won." Pressing to engage rather than just to close distances ensures the team in possession aren't given the time or space to play through otherwise half-hearted pressure. 2. Knowing when to press and when to drop off When discussing how good or bad a team is at pressing, how much they run is often brought up. But the distance a team covers fails to paint the full picture when it comes to the effectiveness of a team's pressing strategy. Liverpool's current boss Andoni Iraola was asked about how he interpreted physical data last year. "It's not 'we run a lot, so we are good,' no," he said. top.title: Ebnoutalib expected to stay at Frankfurt despite rumours of a winter exit
top.description: Ebnoutalib expected to stay at Frankfurt despite rumours of a winter exit It's becoming apparently clear that Younes Ebnoutalib will not be leaving Eintracht Frankfurt during the winter transfer window. Contrary to other sources, Sky Germany understands that a move for the 23-year-old in January is simply out of the question. Earlier in the week, Sport BILD reported that a quick departure was possible, with the striker said to be feeling undervalued at Frankfurt. Whether there will be any further developments regarding this player remains to be seen, but an exit in early 2027 seems off the cards. Borussia Dortmund is fully informed about all the details of a potential summer deal. A transfer fee of €35million is being discussed. On Wednesday, BVB were listed as potential suitors for Ebnoutalib, with Bayern Munich, Juventus and Tottenham Hotspur also keen .

Facing third-and-10 on the Chiefs’ own 9-yard line, Patrick Mahomes threw what was originally called a completed 11-yard pass to Rashee Rice . top.description: Manchester City have a lot of bigger concerns right now but some of Enzo Maresca ’s staff have naturally been conscious of the noise around David Raya . The goalkeeper was not wearing a sling at Tuesday’s Champions League match against Borussia Dortmund, after he had so conspicuously been photographed sporting one on London’s busiest street just two days before. It’s certainly true the injury suffered at Newcastle United is nowhere near as bad as first feared, with contact on a nerve having apparently caused the initial issue. Some on the City side have wondered whether Mikel Arteta is using it to play his usual games. The manager likes to use media and even official squad photos to keep opposition guessing. Arsenal manager Mikel Arteta during the Champions League clash with Dortmund (PA) It would be especially understandable here, since this position could go a long way to deciding Sunday’s game. The entire decision on Raya, in fact, draws out so many of its strands and storylines. Both sides are especially attuned to it since it was as recently as March's Carabao Cup final that Pep Guardiola ’s response to the Kepa Arrizabalaga selection essentially decided that game. It might even have been the Catalan’s last piece of genius in England. Arsenal couldn’t play out of the press without Raya's passing, and City gradually shut them down. The tactical effect of it was so pronounced that it framed the thinking of both clubs ahead of April’s suffocatingly tense Premier League showdown. That 2-1 City win might well go down as one of those influential defeats, rather than decisive victories, because of the effect on Arsenal. top.title: 'You're always allowed to dream' - Marco Rose backs Bournemouth's Europa League ambitions after 10-man comeback against Celta Vigo seals 10th straight victory
top.description: FBL-EUR-C3-CELTA VIGO-BOURNEMOUTH - AFP Bournemouth manager Marco Rose has backed his side's Europa League ambitions after a stunning 10-man comeback against Celta Vigo sealed a club-record 10th straight victory on Thursday. Despite Bafode Diakite's early red card, the Cherries fought back to win 2-1 in Spain and maintain their perfect start to their debut European campaign. Cherries stun Celta in Spain Bournemouth overcame a first-half deficit and a red card to extend their winning streak in Spain . Iago Aspas had curled Celta ahead before Bafode Diakite was dismissed via VAR in the 23rd minute for catching Couhaib Driouech high on the ankle. Second-half goals from Alvaro Rodriguez and substitute Rayan then turned the match around as Celta saw three strikes ruled out for offside. Rose embraces European trophy dream The dramatic turnaround left Bournemouth top of the Europa League table with five wins from five, becoming only the third side to win their opening five major European fixtures after Nuremberg in 1961-62 and Ararat in 1972-73. Already rated among the tournament favourites with a 26 per cent title chance by the Opta supercomputer before kick-off, Rose refused to dampen expectations. Speaking to TNT Sports , Rose said: "You're always allowed to dream. If you get into a competition like this, you want to achieve the best possible things, but we know that there's a long way to go, with many games. "Now it's about getting in the top eight, to avoid even more games for us, as a Premier League club, and then we can see, step by step. Staying humble is good in our situation, and working hard." Remarkable turnaround under German boss Thursday's triumph made Bournemouth the first Premier League team in any competition to win after trailing with 10 men at half-time since Liverpool beat Newcastle United in August 2023. Remarkably, Rose made eight changes from their previous league outing, yet his side improved after the dismissal, firing seven second-half shots compared to three before the interval. Momentum shifted when Rodriguez headed in Amine Adli's inswinging cross, before fellow substitutes Adrien Truffert and Marcus Tavernier combined to set up Rayan's winner. It caps an extraordinary revival for Andoni Iraola's successor, who sat just above the relegation zone without a league win after losing 5-1 to Chelsea on October 10, only to reel off 10 straight wins while scoring at least twice in every game. Quick turnaround awaits at Fulham Rose now faces another rapid turnaround as fifth-placed Bournemouth travel to Fulham on Sunday in the Premier League. Sitting just four points off second place, the Cherries will be eager to carry their relentless momentum back into domestic action. Securing another victory in west London would keep their remarkable winning streak alive while easing the pressure of juggling European and league commitments.

top.title: Bournemouth make history! Marco Rose's men set unprecedented English record in Europe after comeback win over Celta Vigo
top.description: Real Club Celta v AFC Bournemouth - UEFA Europa League 2026/27 League Phase MD5 - Getty Images Sport Bournemouth’s fairy-tale start to life in continental competition reached new heights on Thursday night as they secured a historic victory on Spanish soil. Marco Rose’s side showed incredible resilience to overcome both a goal deficit and a first-half red card to maintain their flawless record in the Europa League. Ten-man Bournemouth stage stunning second-half turnaround Iago Aspas curled Celta Vigo ahead before Bafode Diakite saw red in the 24th minute for a poorly timed tackle, leaving the visitors a goal and a player down at half-time. Despite playing over an hour with 10 men, Bournemouth controlled the game after the interval. Amine Adli crossed early in the second half for Alvaro Rodriguez to head an equaliser, before substitute Rayan swept in the winner 12 minutes from time to seal a 2-1 victory . Adli hails character after dramatic comeback Speaking to TNT Sports after the match, Adli praised his side's resilience in Spain. "We showed a lot of character," he said. "It's amazing to come back in this way and go back home with the three points." He also detailed his thinking behind the assist for the equaliser. "I was looking for someone in the box," Adli added. "I know Alvaro is very good in the air and he was in a good position so I just tried to deliver a dangerous ball towards the far post." Historic milestone extends club-record winning streak Bournemouth are now the first English club to win their opening five European games, and only the third in major continental competitions after Nurnberg in 1961-62 and Ararat in 1972-73. The triumph also extends their club-record winning run to 10 matches across all competitions, complementing their fifth-place Premier League standing. Adli credited the squad's half-time belief for driving the turnaround. "I think it was down to the mentality of the players. From the moment we conceded the goal, and even after the red card, we always believed in ourselves," he noted. "What's fantastic is that in the dressing room, even before the coach started speaking, everybody was saying, 'we can do this.' Everyone was motivated and still believed we could turn things around." Knockout qualification within reach for Europa League leaders Topping the Europa League league phase table, Bournemouth have one foot in the knockout rounds. Sustaining this unshakeable mentality will be crucial as Rose's men look to safeguard both their European summit and their strong domestic position.

top.title: Man City owners should be forced to sell, say rival club chiefs
top.description: The independent commission is yet to decide on a sanction for Manchester City [Getty Images] Manchester City's owners must be forced to sell up as punishment for breaking financial rules, senior figures at Premier League clubs have told BBC Sport. This week, the chair of the Independent Football Regulator (IFR) David Kogan claimed he has the "stomach" to take action against City, who deny wrongdoing and have appealed. The IFR has the power to remove directors of a club if they are deemed unsuitable, and even force a sale in the most serious cases. Now, executives at three top-flight rivals have told the BBC that they believe this is the appropriate punishment for City, who were found guilty of breaching Premier League financial regulations rules between 2009 and 2018, and failing to co-operate with an investigation. Premier League clubs to cover legal costs if Man City sponsors sue Rival clubs want range of punishments for Man City The independent commission has yet to decide on a sanction that could range from a fine, to a points deduction, the stripping of past titles, or even expulsion from the league. But speaking on condition of anonymity, one executive claimed they are among a group of clubs who feel that City's punishment will be irrelevant unless the owners are also forced to sell. They added that anything less will make them question why they are funding the regulator through a levy. In comments that reveal the level of anger felt by some of City's rivals, another claimed the rule breaches had undermined the league's credibility, and that they would not be able to draw a line under the scandal and move on if the owners were allowed to stay. The club were found guilty of inflating revenues and disguising losses by £900m through "sham" commercial arrangements. Manchester City's owners are Abu Dhabi United Group - a private investment company belonging to United Arab Emirates vice-president and deputy Prime Minister Sheikh Mansour. The executive who spoke anonymously said that clubs had been asked by the Premier League to refrain from publicly revealing their views on sanctions, and let the process run its course, although some are said to have privately made their opinions clear to IFR officials. They acknowledged that some clubs were less opinionated about a punishment. Other clubs the BBC approached declined to comment, or said they were willing for the independent commission panel and IFR to reach their own conclusions following the publication of the commission's ruling in September. But the fact that some clubs want the unprecedented sanction of a forced sale will put pressure on Kogan to mete out the harshest penalty possible in what is being seen as a defining test of the watchdog just over a year after it was established. It also comes amid mounting questions over whether wider UAE trade and investment in UK projects could be impacted by such a move. top.description: ESPN and Kirk Herbstreit are set to talk about a new contract in the near future Getty ESPN and Kirk Herbstreit will reportedly talk about a new contract after the college football season Getty Kirk Herbstreit recently signed a new deal with Amazon Prime Video Getty Kirk Herbstreit has been the face of ESPN’s college football coverage for three decades. Whether that continues past this season is now a fair question. Herbstreit’s ESPN contract runs out after the current college football season. On Wednesday, Front Office Sports’ Ryan Glasspiegel reported that Herbstreit and the network were closing in on a long-term deal. However, ESPN wasn’t ready to commit to that just yet. The network quickly pushed back on the report, and its timeline for a decision is clear: it’s waiting until the season is over. ESPN Shoots Down Report on Kirk Herbstreit Contract Getty ESPN and Kirk Herbstreit will reportedly talk about a new contract after the college football season It’s not often a network publicly shuts down a report that it’s about to keep its biggest college football star. top.title: 2027: 2Baba backs ‘rig and die’ slogan, demands severe penalties
top.description: Nigerian music star, Innocent Idibia, popularly known as 2Baba, has backed the controversial “rig and die” slogan associated with the Nigeria Democratic Congress (NDC), saying anyone caught manipulating election results in 2027 should face severe punishment. The singer, however, cautioned against innocent people being victimised in the process, insisting that elections should not be treated as warfare. He made the remarks on Thursday during an interview on Nigeria Info 99.3, where he described Nigeria’s political atmosphere as tense and said the slogan reflected growing public frustration over the country’s situation. “You know, when the situation gets to a certain point, like right now, we’re on a very mountainous keg of gunpowder right now. Desperate times make people make some kinds of statements. “The statement sounds correct, right? It sounds correct. It should be like that, actually. For the circumstances. Like, if you rig, the punishments will be very severe to deter people from rigging,” 2Baba said. The singer said he saw nothing wrong with the slogan, arguing that stringent penalties would discourage electoral malpractice. “The statement itself is ‘rig and die’. I don’t see anything that’s wrong with it. It’s like saying embezzlement and die. Now, there’s that penalty for embezzlement in China,” he said. 2Baba also called for severe consequences for kidnappers, particularly those targeting schools, arguing that the absence of adequate deterrence had allowed criminal activities to persist. “We’re in a state where we need serious deterrence for anybody who kidnaps in our schools to face serious consequences, so that others will not do it. Because it’s getting too much and people are just getting away with everything,” he said. The ‘African Queen’ crooner said the slogan reflected the level of frustration among Nigerians but warned against punishing people without evidence of wrongdoing. “For me, the statement itself shows the level of frustration. It shows the level of how things have gone bad. So, for me, I don’t see anything wrong with that statement. “I just don’t want innocent people to get caught up in the process of this,” he added. During the interview, the presenter recalled 2Baba’s longstanding advocacy for peaceful electoral participation, including his message urging Nigerians to vote rather than fight during elections. Asked about Nigerians who might sell their votes because of economic hardship, the singer described the situation as unfortunate, noting that people facing difficult conditions could easily become vulnerable to manipulation. He also called for proper reorientation, urging Nigerians to address internal challenges rather than allow external interests to influence the country. top.description: Carlos Ulberg UFC Getty Eugene Bareman, the head coach of UFC light heavyweight champion Carlos Ulberg at City Kickboxing, isn’t worried about Ulberg being stripped. Bareman said this week that Ulberg will not fight his teammate Navajo Stirling for the UFC light heavyweight title, even though there is a good argument that they are the top two fighters in their weight class. While some fans have suggested that Ulberg should be stripped because he won’t fight Stirling, Bareman said he’s not worried about that happening. Carlos Ulberg Won’t Be Stripped, Says Coach Speaking to the New Zealand Herald, Bareman said that he’s not concerned about Ulberg being stripped since there have been similar situations between two teammates not wanting to fight in the UFC and the champion not losing their belt. “There’s precedent for this all over the UFC (not stripping Ulberg),” Bareman said (via Bloody Elbow ). In fact, Bareman doesn’t even think the UFC matchmakers will offer the fight, since he’s made it clear that both men won’t fight each other. “No, because there has to be a fight on the table and it has to be offered. Why would they offer us a fight when we’ve said that. They’re not going to offer us a fight if we said that we’re not going to fight,” Bareman said. “It just wouldn’t come across the table because they know that, we’re just standing on our ground here.” Dana White’s Reaction Will Be Interesting The UFC is enjoying a rare off week this weekend for Thanksgiving, so reporters haven’t had the opportunity to ask UFC president Dana White what his thoughts on this situation are. While it’s not fair to put words in White’s mouth, we do know that White has said many times that he views the UFC as an opportunity to make money for yourself and help your family have a great life. For Stirling to make the most money possible, he would need to become the UFC light heavyweight champion, which won’t happen if he is unwilling to fight Ulberg, which appears to be the case, as Bareman has squashed the fight. top.title: The Curious Case of Everton Defender Jarrad Branthwaite
top.description: Less said about Brentford away the better. Everton defender Jarrad Branthwaite, the lad from Carlisle is a hot topic at the best of times. The curious case of Jarrad Branthwaite is upon us. The positives Let’s get the positive things out of the way. Jarrad Branthwaite is a very good and classy defender, he makes Everton very much better when he plays and considerably worse when he doesn’t. Next to James Tarkowski, who unfortunately misses the game against Liverpool due to suspension , he has shown that he has all the attributes to be one of the best English defenders for years to come. He is quick, loves a tackle and has the brains of a defender a lot more his senior. It is a testament to the young lad that he has been linked with moves away from the club, for bigger and maybe better. Tyrique George On Joining Everton, David Moyes, and Thierno Barry Everton winger Tyrique George has been discussing joining Everton on loan and permanently, manager David Moyes, and Thierno Barry's dancing. The negatives The negative part of Jarrad Branthwaite, is that it seems he is made of biscuits. Jarrad has had a terrible time with injuries, namely his hamstring. Jarrad missed big chunks of the season last year due to this reoccurring injury. To David Moyes’ credit, he has managed the injuries of Jarrad very well, and has taken him off, left him out when he was ‘half fit’ much unlike the managers before him, who would just play him. Big clubs will be put off by this, as it seems he can’t get a full season under his belt, and maybe that is the factor of how Everton have kept him for so long. Also, the fact of how Everton play their game might put off the suitors. Everton defend deep, that is a well-known fact, so positioning is key for Branthwaite’s game. Better footballing teams will play further up the pitch, would this suit Branthwaite as the ball over the top has been known to kill Everton. Look at Harry Maguire at Leicester, then on to Man United, it shows even the best defenders struggle with the high line. Everton Have Centre-Back Decision To Make: It's Simple Everton manager David Moyes has a decision to make as to who he plays at right-back and centre-back against Liverpool due to James Tarkowski's suspension. The difficulties One thing that needs to come to an end, playing Branthwaite at left back. For someone with Jarrad’s brain, he does get sucked in and out of the left back position and seems to drift over more central. This is not necessarily Jarrad’s fault, he is just being told where to play. You can see the whole crowd, also, grimace every time he goes down off a challenge, whether it be for two seconds or two minutes minutes. We always think the worst. Hopefully, the injuries become less frequent and he can lead the back for many years to come. With success though, we will see the vultures circling for the Carlisle lad. One thing is for sure, Everton need Jarrad fit and firing come Sunday vs Liverpool. Here is hoping!

The conference, themed “Digital Identity: A Catalyst for Financial Inclusion, Trust and Growth,” will bring together policymakers, regulators, financial services leaders and technology innovators to examine the role of identity infrastructure in Nigeria’s digital financial ecosystem. Speaking at a press conference on the theme of the conference, Chairman of CeBIH, Mrs. Abidemi Asunmo, said the future of financial services and the broader digital economy depended significantly on reliable, secure and accessible digital identity infrastructure. “A trusted digital identity ecosystem has implications far beyond registration and identification. It can help address some of the structural barriers to financial inclusion.’’ Gbolahan Oluwatobiloba, Lagos State Coordinator, NIMC, said identity was the foundation of economic development, security and trust. “Identity is the foundation of everything, not just the financial sector, the security sector or the identity ecosystem. When you remove identity, your security will be affected, because how do you secure people you don’t know?” he said. Vice Chairman of CeBIH and Chairman of the Conference Planning Committee, Abednigo Ugwueke, said participants would examine how trusted digital identity could improve customer onboarding, strengthen Know Your Customer processes, enhance identity verification, reduce fraud and expand access to financial services. The conference is expected to feature key government and industry personalities, including NIMC Director-General, Engr. Abisoye Coker-Odusote; Executive Chairman of the Nigeria Revenue Service, Dr. Zach Adedeji; National Commissioner and Chief Executive Officer of the Nigeria Data Protection Commission, Dr. Vincent Olatunji; and Comptroller-General of the Nigeria Immigration Service, Kemi Nanna Nandap. nigeria.title: Fountain of Life Church challenges bench warrant against Pastor Jimmy Odukoya
nigeria.description: The Fountain of Life Church has raised concerns over the issuance of a bench warrant against its Senior Pastor, Jimmy Odukoya, by the Lagos State High Court, questioning the procedure leading to the order. In a statement dated November 26, 2026, the church said the development followed proceedings before Justice O. O. Adewunmi-Oshin, which also culminated in the judge’s recusal from the case. The church claimed that Odukoya had not been formally served with the restraining order, originating processes and accompanying documents, either personally or through substituted service, as directed by the court. It also alleged that directives contained in the court’s orders of November 18 and 23 concerning the service of the documents remained unfulfilled. According to the church, its legal representatives had already filed a Notice of Appeal and two separate motions challenging the orders, their enforcement, the court’s jurisdiction and the contempt proceedings. The church further claimed that the matter was not listed on the court’s cause list for November 26 and that members of the media were asked to leave the courtroom before the bench warrant was issued. It said the warrant was issued without the court first determining the pending applications, after which the presiding judge recused herself. “These developments occurred within eight days of the initial ex parte order and before 1 December 2026, the date originally fixed by the court for mention,” the statement said. The church described the circumstances as raising serious questions about due process, fair hearing and the administration of justice. It added that its lawyers were challenging the orders and related procedural and jurisdictional issues before the appropriate courts, including the Court of Appeal. Clarifying the implications of the warrant, the church said its issuance did not amount to a conviction or a final determination of the substantive leadership dispute. The church also maintained that Odukoya remained its duly appointed Senior Pastor and Chairman of the Board of Trustees, describing the position as part of the issues being pursued through the judicial process. It urged members and the general public to remain calm, united and prayerful, adding that it would exhaust all available legal remedies within the Nigerian judicial system. The president pointed out that the gesture would also be extended to the immediate families of the civilians on board the aircraft. “In addition to the flats, these officers would receive from this government N100m each,” he said. He assured the bereaved families that the government would remain committed to supporting them beyond the memorial ceremony. “Long after the wreaths have faded, our commitment to these families must remain evergreen,” Tinubu said. The president also assured Nigerians that the October 5 aircraft crash would be thoroughly investigated, promising that the findings would inform improvements in military and civilian aviation safety. “I assure the grieving nation that this accident will be thoroughly investigated. We will seek answers. We will learn the lessons. We will strengthen our military and civilian aviation safety standards. Our operational procedures and our institutional accountability will be strengthened. “We owe them the truth, and we will honour that debt,” he said. nigeria.description: …As Uko urges peace, unity, stronger grassroots mobilisation A chieftain of the All Progressives Congress (APC), Chief John Ewhubare Siakpere, has called on political leaders and stakeholders in the Aghalokpe axis of Okpe Local Government Area to unite and intensify grassroots mobilisation to secure victory for President Bola Tinubu, Governor Sheriff Oborevwori and other APC candidates in the 2027 general elections. Siakpere, a member of the Delta State APC Campaign Council, made the call on Thursday when he hosted APC leaders and stakeholders from the Aghalokpe axis at his country home, urging them to put aside personal differences and work collectively for the success of the party. The APC chieftain, who is the Omo-Eni of Okpe Kingdom and a member of the Delta State APC Campaign Council, said Okpe’s political influence would depend largely on the ability of its leaders to speak with one voice and mobilise support at the grassroots. He urged the people to work for the re-election of President Tinubu and Governor Oborevwori, stressing that the party must secure victory at all levels in 2027. According to him, Governor Oborevwori’s decision to lead Delta State into the APC had further strengthened the party’s political standing, making it imperative for leaders and members to rally behind his administration and support its re-election bid. He said winning elections required more than political declarations, insisting that party leaders must maintain regular contact with the people, understand their concerns and take the APC’s message to every community. On the economic reforms of the Tinubu administration, Siakpere acknowledged the hardship Nigerians were experiencing, particularly the rising cost of food, transportation and other essential commodities. He, however, urged party leaders to explain the rationale behind the reforms, including the removal of fuel subsidy, while also emphasising the need for the government to ensure that the measures translate into tangible improvements in the lives of citizens. He noted that the savings from subsidy removal had increased the resources available to governments to meet their obligations and execute development projects. Turning to Delta State, Siakpere commended Governor Oborevwori for his investments in infrastructure, particularly road construction, bridges and flyovers. He said the engagement of reputable construction firms, including Julius Berger, reflected the administration’s determination to deliver durable infrastructure, adding that communities in Delta Central, including Okpe and neighbouring areas, were benefiting from ongoing projects. The APC chieftain urged party leaders in Aghalokpe to take the campaign to every ward, community and polling unit, ensuring that women, youths and first-time voters were actively involved. He also cautioned against internal wrangling and personal interests, calling for peaceful, issue-based campaigns capable of strengthening the party ahead of the elections.

entertainment.title: M.Inc PR Joins Industry Stakeholders to Explore Africa’s Credit Economy at ACE 2026
entertainment.description: A cross section of industry leaders and stakeholders during the fourth edition of Africa Credit Expo 2026 held on Friday, 13 November 2026, at the J. F. Ade Ajayi Main Auditorium, University of Lagos. What will it take to make credit more accessible to African businesses and individuals? At the fourth edition of Africa Credit Expo (ACE) 202 6, stakeholders across financial services, technology, policy, investment and entrepreneurship examined the role of reliable credit information, financial inclusion and collaboration in expanding access to capital. Powered by CreditRegistry and supported by Afreximbank , the Expo was held on Friday, 13 November 2026, at the J. F. Ade Ajayi Main Auditorium, University of Lagos. Themed “Reimagining Africa’s Credit Economy: Unlocking Capital, Trust and Opportunity,” the event provided a platform for conversations on the systems, innovations and partnerships shaping the future of credit across the continent. Building Trust and Expanding Access to Capital Discussions at the Expo explored the role of credible credit information in building trust between lenders and borrowers. Reliable data enables financial institutions to assess risk more effectively and make informed lending decisions, while individuals and businesses with established credit histories are better positioned to demonstrate their credit worthiness. The conversations also considered the financing constraints facing micro, small and medium-sized enterprises (MSMEs). Despite their contribution to employment and economic activity, many small businesses continue to encounter barriers to affordable financing. Improving access to relevant financial products and strengthening credit information systems remain important to addressing these gaps. Technology, Financial Inclusion and the Next Generation Digital innovation and data intelligence featured prominently in discussions about the future of credit. Alternative credit assessment approaches have the potential to broaden access for individuals and businesses with limited formal credit histories. However, the expansion of digital financial services must be accompanied by responsible lending practices, consumer protection and transparency. The Expo also placed attention on young people through student-focused sessions and discussions on financial literacy. These conversations connected access to credit with the need for individuals to understand financial management, borrowing and long-term wealth creation. This focus reflects the February 2026 memorandum of understanding between CreditRegistry and the University of Lagos, through its Entrepreneurship and Skills Development Centre (ESDC), to integrate the Africa Consumer Credit Academy (ACCA) curriculum into the Centre’s programmes. The initiative is intended to strengthen financial literacy through learning opportunities, mentorship, certification and engagement with industry. entertainment.title: As Nigeria Rethinks Teacher Education, Tunji Olowolafe Makes a Case for Better-Prepared Educators
entertainment.description: What makes a good teacher? Beyond knowing a subject, a good teacher can understand students, inspire confidence, and help young people discover what they are capable of becoming. It was this broader responsibility of educators that Dr. Tunji Olowolafe explored while delivering the 2026 Convocation Lecture at the Sikiru Adetona College of Education, Science and Technology (SACOETEC), Omu-Ajose, Ogun State. Speaking on Monday, 23 November 2026, on the theme “The Dual-Mandate NCE-Degree Programme: Prospects, Challenges and the Future of Teacher Education in Nigeria,” he described the programme as an important opportunity to reposition teacher education. For decades, Colleges of Education depended on university affiliations to award Bachelor’s degrees, despite many possessing the academic capacity to run such programmes. The Federal Colleges of Education Act 2023 changed this, empowering eligible institutions to award degrees independently. Under the Dual-Mandate programme, students can complete three years of NCE training and proceed to another two years for a Bachelor’s degree in Education. Dr. Olowolafe explained that combining practical teaching skills with deeper academic knowledge would produce better-prepared educators. However, he cautioned that institutional autonomy must be supported by sustained funding, improved curricula and professional development. With Nigeria facing an estimated shortage of one million teachers, he also called for greater integration of vocational education, artificial intelligence and digital skills into learning. “AI can explain a quadratic equation at midnight, but it cannot offer the steady, empathetic guidance of a caring adult,” he said, emphasizing that artificial intelligence must complement, not replace, the human qualities of effective teaching. During the lecture, Dr. Olowolafe announced that the Tunji Olowolafe Foundation would establish a fully equipped, solar-powered Gbemisola Olowolafe Memorial ICT Centre (GOMTECH) with high-speed internet connectivity at SACOETEC. The Foundation is also committed to recognising academic excellence and outstanding teaching at the College. This includes recognising the College’s first-class degree graduates and NCE distinction holders, alongside the overall best NCE and degree graduates. Lecturers, selected based on student ratings, will also be honoured for their teaching contributions. The initiative builds on the Foundation’s existing investment in education, including Project Digi-Teach at Ekiti State University and GOMTECH in Are-Ekiti. For Dr. Olowolafe, the commitment to educators is also deeply personal. His mother was a teacher, his elder sister taught for years at Baptist Academy, Lagos, and his late wife, Gbemisola Olowolafe, was a lifelong educator. entertainment.title: Nollywood Legend Pete Edochie Passes Away at 79
entertainment.description: Nollywood icon Pete Edochie, MON, who passed away at the age of 79 in Enugu. Photo Credit: Pete Edochie/Instagram Nollywood and the wider African entertainment community are mourning the loss of one of their most respected screen icons, Pete Edochie , MON, who passed away on Wednesday, 25 November 2026,at the age of 79. According to an official statement released on behalf of the family by his eldest son, Leo Pete Edochie , the veteran actor and retired broadcaster departed this life at 12:30 a.m. in Enugu, Nigeria, following a protracted battle with prostate cancer. Born on 7 March 1947 in Zaria, Kaduna State, and hailing from Akamnato, Ifite Nteje in Anambra State, Pete Edochie began his career in broadcasting long before becoming a household name on television and cinema screens. At age 20, in 1967, he joined the Eastern Nigeria Broadcasting Service (ENBS)—later the Anambra Broadcasting Service (ABS)—rising steadily through the ranks to serve as Director of Programmes and Deputy Managing Director. His defining breakthrough came in 1987 when he portrayed the fierce, tragic hero Okonkwo in the Nigerian Television Authority’s (NTA) acclaimed television adaptation of Chinua Achebe ‘s Things Fall Apart. His commanding presence and deep, resonant voice earned him international recognition—including a dedicated delegation interview from the BBC—and cemented his place in Nigerian television history. Over a screen career spanning nearly four decades, Pete Edochie became synonymous with authority,traditional wisdom, and unforgettable Igbo proverbs. Whether playing stern monarchs, principled elders, or complex patriarchs, he delivered every line with unmistakable gravitas. His extensive filmography includes standout appearances in classics and modern hits alike, such as Things Fall Apart (1987), Igodo (1999), Egg of Life (2003), Oracle (2003), Billionaires Club (2003), End of Money (2005), Lionheart (2018)—where he starred as Chief Ernest Obiagu alongside Genevieve Nnaji—Unroyal (2020), and Foreigner’s God (2022). In recognition of his immense contributions to Nigerian arts and culture, he was conferred with the national honour of Member of the Order of the Niger (MON) in 2003 by former President Olusegun Obasanjo,alongside the Africa Magic Viewers’ Choice Awards (AMVCA) Industry Merit Award and lifetime achievement honours from the Africa Film Academy and the African Film Festival (TAFF). sports.title: What makes or breaks a high press?
sports.description: Alexander Isak and Florian Wirtz spearhead Liverpool's press under Andoni Iraola [Getty Images] A good high press has been the basis for some of the most successful sides in modern football but a well-oiled pressing machine has many moving parts - all requiring close attention. When an out-of-possession plan is implemented poorly, entire seasons can fall apart. So, what determines whether a press works or fails? And how are the always-adapting Premier League teams exploiting high presses this season? 1. Establishing intent When a team decides to press, they must first establish their intention. This informs how the players act. Speaking to DAZN Portugal , Brighton manager Fabian Hurzeler was asked about whether a good press relied more on physicality or courage. "A really good question," he began. "When you want to press high you need the courage and mindset to do it. Our mindset is we press to score, we don't just press to win the ball back." In coaching, clarity is key - particularly when it comes to creating alignment in the squad and Hurzeler is deliberate in simplifying big ideas when delivering messages to his players, a skill he practised as a radio pundit during the World Cup. "[Punditry] helps you as a coach in that you have to summarise things in a short and easy way so that everyone understands," he said. "Football might get more complex but simplicity counts." Hurzeler's "pressing to score" is a phrase that communicates many ideas in a memorable three words: intensity, being proactive, and immediate forward-thinking on winning the ball. It also frames pressing in a way that makes it easy for attackers to buy into, in the form of goals. "You want commitment from everyone on the pitch," Hurzeler explained. "If just one has doubts, the whole press is gone." The Red Bull school of coaching uses a similarly succinct phrase - "the last step" to address these ideas around intention, collectiveness and aggression. Summarised by Tactx , whose coaches have worked under the Red Bull model, the last step refers to "players [being] coached to attack through the opponent, using the final step to lunge aggressively at the ball". "This action commits the defender fully and is often the decisive moment that allows possession to be won." Pressing to engage rather than just to close distances ensures the team in possession aren't given the time or space to play through otherwise half-hearted pressure. 2. Knowing when to press and when to drop off When discussing how good or bad a team is at pressing, how much they run is often brought up. But the distance a team covers fails to paint the full picture when it comes to the effectiveness of a team's pressing strategy. sports.title: 'You're always allowed to dream' - Marco Rose backs Bournemouth's Europa League ambitions after 10-man comeback against Celta Vigo seals 10th straight victory
sports.description: FBL-EUR-C3-CELTA VIGO-BOURNEMOUTH - AFP Bournemouth manager Marco Rose has backed his side's Europa League ambitions after a stunning 10-man comeback against Celta Vigo sealed a club-record 10th straight victory on Thursday. Despite Bafode Diakite's early red card, the Cherries fought back to win 2-1 in Spain and maintain their perfect start to their debut European campaign. Cherries stun Celta in Spain Bournemouth overcame a first-half deficit and a red card to extend their winning streak in Spain . Iago Aspas had curled Celta ahead before Bafode Diakite was dismissed via VAR in the 23rd minute for catching Couhaib Driouech high on the ankle. Second-half goals from Alvaro Rodriguez and substitute Rayan then turned the match around as Celta saw three strikes ruled out for offside. Rose embraces European trophy dream The dramatic turnaround left Bournemouth top of the Europa League table with five wins from five, becoming only the third side to win their opening five major European fixtures after Nuremberg in 1961-62 and Ararat in 1972-73. Already rated among the tournament favourites with a 26 per cent title chance by the Opta supercomputer before kick-off, Rose refused to dampen expectations. Speaking to TNT Sports , Rose said: "You're always allowed to dream. If you get into a competition like this, you want to achieve the best possible things, but we know that there's a long way to go, with many games. "Now it's about getting in the top eight, to avoid even more games for us, as a Premier League club, and then we can see, step by step. Staying humble is good in our situation, and working hard." Remarkable turnaround under German boss Thursday's triumph made Bournemouth the first Premier League team in any competition to win after trailing with 10 men at half-time since Liverpool beat Newcastle United in August 2023. Remarkably, Rose made eight changes from their previous league outing, yet his side improved after the dismissal, firing seven second-half shots compared to three before the interval. Momentum shifted when Rodriguez headed in Amine Adli's inswinging cross, before fellow substitutes Adrien Truffert and Marcus Tavernier combined to set up Rayan's winner. It caps an extraordinary revival for Andoni Iraola's successor, who sat just above the relegation zone without a league win after losing 5-1 to Chelsea on October 10, only to reel off 10 straight wins while scoring at least twice in every game. Quick turnaround awaits at Fulham Rose now faces another rapid turnaround as fifth-placed Bournemouth travel to Fulham on Sunday in the Premier League. Sitting just four points off second place, the Cherries will be eager to carry their relentless momentum back into domestic action. Securing another victory in west London would keep their remarkable winning streak alive while easing the pressure of juggling European and league commitments.

sports.description: The independent commission is yet to decide on a sanction for Manchester City [Getty Images] Manchester City's owners must be forced to sell up as punishment for breaking financial rules, senior figures at Premier League clubs have told BBC Sport. This week, the chair of the Independent Football Regulator (IFR) David Kogan claimed he has the "stomach" to take action against City, who deny wrongdoing and have appealed. The IFR has the power to remove directors of a club if they are deemed unsuitable, and even force a sale in the most serious cases. Now, executives at three top-flight rivals have told the BBC that they believe this is the appropriate punishment for City, who were found guilty of breaching Premier League financial regulations rules between 2009 and 2018, and failing to co-operate with an investigation. Premier League clubs to cover legal costs if Man City sponsors sue Rival clubs want range of punishments for Man City The independent commission has yet to decide on a sanction that could range from a fine, to a points deduction, the stripping of past titles, or even expulsion from the league. But speaking on condition of anonymity, one executive claimed they are among a group of clubs who feel that City's punishment will be irrelevant unless the owners are also forced to sell. They added that anything less will make them question why they are funding the regulator through a levy. In comments that reveal the level of anger felt by some of City's rivals, another claimed the rule breaches had undermined the league's credibility, and that they would not be able to draw a line under the scandal and move on if the owners were allowed to stay. The club were found guilty of inflating revenues and disguising losses by £900m through "sham" commercial arrangements. Manchester City's owners are Abu Dhabi United Group - a private investment company belonging to United Arab Emirates vice-president and deputy Prime Minister Sheikh Mansour. The executive who spoke anonymously said that clubs had been asked by the Premier League to refrain from publicly revealing their views on sanctions, and let the process run its course, although some are said to have privately made their opinions clear to IFR officials. They acknowledged that some clubs were less opinionated about a punishment. Other clubs the BBC approached declined to comment, or said they were willing for the independent commission panel and IFR to reach their own conclusions following the publication of the commission's ruling in September. But the fact that some clubs want the unprecedented sanction of a forced sale will put pressure on Kogan to mete out the harshest penalty possible in what is being seen as a defining test of the watchdog just over a year after it was established. sports.title: Coach Not Worried About UFC Stripping Carlos Ulberg
sports.description: Carlos Ulberg UFC Getty Eugene Bareman, the head coach of UFC light heavyweight champion Carlos Ulberg at City Kickboxing, isn’t worried about Ulberg being stripped. Bareman said this week that Ulberg will not fight his teammate Navajo Stirling for the UFC light heavyweight title, even though there is a good argument that they are the top two fighters in their weight class. While some fans have suggested that Ulberg should be stripped because he won’t fight Stirling, Bareman said he’s not worried about that happening. Carlos Ulberg Won’t Be Stripped, Says Coach Speaking to the New Zealand Herald, Bareman said that he’s not concerned about Ulberg being stripped since there have been similar situations between two teammates not wanting to fight in the UFC and the champion not losing their belt. “There’s precedent for this all over the UFC (not stripping Ulberg),” Bareman said (via Bloody Elbow ). In fact, Bareman doesn’t even think the UFC matchmakers will offer the fight, since he’s made it clear that both men won’t fight each other. “No, because there has to be a fight on the table and it has to be offered. Why would they offer us a fight when we’ve said that. They’re not going to offer us a fight if we said that we’re not going to fight,” Bareman said. “It just wouldn’t come across the table because they know that, we’re just standing on our ground here.” Dana White’s Reaction Will Be Interesting The UFC is enjoying a rare off week this weekend for Thanksgiving, so reporters haven’t had the opportunity to ask UFC president Dana White what his thoughts on this situation are. sports.title: The Curious Case of Everton Defender Jarrad Branthwaite
sports.description: Less said about Brentford away the better. Everton defender Jarrad Branthwaite, the lad from Carlisle is a hot topic at the best of times. The curious case of Jarrad Branthwaite is upon us. The positives Let’s get the positive things out of the way. Jarrad Branthwaite is a very good and classy defender, he makes Everton very much better when he plays and considerably worse when he doesn’t. Next to James Tarkowski, who unfortunately misses the game against Liverpool due to suspension , he has shown that he has all the attributes to be one of the best English defenders for years to come. He is quick, loves a tackle and has the brains of a defender a lot more his senior. It is a testament to the young lad that he has been linked with moves away from the club, for bigger and maybe better. Tyrique George On Joining Everton, David Moyes, and Thierno Barry Everton winger Tyrique George has been discussing joining Everton on loan and permanently, manager David Moyes, and Thierno Barry's dancing. The negatives The negative part of Jarrad Branthwaite, is that it seems he is made of biscuits. Jarrad has had a terrible time with injuries, namely his hamstring. Jarrad missed big chunks of the season last year due to this reoccurring injury. To David Moyes’ credit, he has managed the injuries of Jarrad very well, and has taken him off, left him out when he was ‘half fit’ much unlike the managers before him, who would just play him. Big clubs will be put off by this, as it seems he can’t get a full season under his belt, and maybe that is the factor of how Everton have kept him for so long. Also, the fact of how Everton play their game might put off the suitors. Everton defend deep, that is a well-known fact, so positioning is key for Branthwaite’s game. Better footballing teams will play further up the pitch, would this suit Branthwaite as the ball over the top has been known to kill Everton. Look at Harry Maguire at Leicester, then on to Man United, it shows even the best defenders struggle with the high line. Everton Have Centre-Back Decision To Make: It's Simple Everton manager David Moyes has a decision to make as to who he plays at right-back and centre-back against Liverpool due to James Tarkowski's suspension. The difficulties One thing that needs to come to an end, playing Branthwaite at left back. For someone with Jarrad’s brain, he does get sucked in and out of the left back position and seems to drift over more central. This is not necessarily Jarrad’s fault, he is just being told where to play. You can see the whole crowd, also, grimace every time he goes down off a challenge, whether it be for two seconds or two minutes minutes. We always think the worst. Hopefully, the injuries become less frequent and he can lead the back for many years to come. With success though, we will see the vultures circling for the Carlisle lad. One thing is for sure, Everton need Jarrad fit and firing come Sunday vs Liverpool. Here is hoping!

Los Blancos could not get going in the first half, with the Dutch side looking far superior. The Portuguese manager is now considering making one of those adjustments a more regular feature of his system. The transformation was remarkable, with both Bellingham and Guler getting into advanced positions and offering plenty in terms of creativity and goalscoring. After the game, Mourinho highlighted the midfield adjustment as one of the main reasons for the second-half turnaround. technology.title: AWS adds virtual iPhones to its cloud
technology.description: AWS now offers two new types of cloudy computers: emulated Androids and simulated iPhones. The cloudy colossus announced both virtual offerings on Wednesday. They’re part of its Device Farm service, which previously saw AWS offer developers the chance to test their software on actual iOS and Android devices that reside in the Amazonian cloud. AWS will now also host virtual devices running Android and iOS. AWS touts the virtual mobile devices as superior to physical devices. “With virtual devices, you can shift testing left to stages that need high speed and volume, such as pull requests, code merges, and smoke tests, and keep real devices for later stages that need high fidelity, such as regression and release testing,” the cloudy business unit argues in its launch announcement. AWS also says developers can get to work faster on a virtual iPhone or Pixel. “Virtual devices running the latest device and OS typically start in seconds, and others start in around a minute,” the outfit argues. That may sound appetizing, but Amazon’s menu of virtual devices is short and bland. When The Register logged on as an AWS user, the only emulated Android phone listed was a Google Pixel 10, running Android 15, 16, or 17. An emulated Pixel tablet running Android 17 is also on the menu. At the time of writing, we could find only a virtual iPhone 16, running iOS 18.6, 23.61, and 27.0. Analyst firm Counterpoint’s list of the world’s top 10 best-selling smartphones in Q2 of 2026 does not include a single Pixel device. The iPhone 16 occupies 10 th place. iPhone 17 models occupy the first, second, third, and seventh place on the list. AWS might excite more developers if it adds emulators for the Samsung Galaxy S26 Ultra, Galaxy A07 4G, A17 5G, A17 4G, and Galaxy S26, as they occupy the fourth, fifth, sixth, eighth and ninth places on Counterpoint’s list. Amazon’s choice of a Pixel tablet is also an oddity given analyst firm IDC doesn’t list Google among its top five tablet vendors . Amazon does offer physical Galaxy A17 devices and three versions of the iPhone 17. But Device Farm doesn’t offer any foldable devices, meaning developers struggling to wrap their heads around the iPhone Duo will need either ask Apple for a loaner or shell out $2,000 to acquire one. At least developers don’t have to change behavior to access the few virtual devices AWS offers, as existing Device Farm APIs and test frameworks will work on real or notional machines. ®

technology.title: Free e-government platform that serves two billion people in ten countries has critical SQL injection bug
technology.description: India’s free e-government platform has a critical SQL injection flaw that thousands of organizations must patch to protect up to two billion citizens. The platform is called the Digital Infrastructure for Governance (Impact and Transformation) – aka DIGIT – and is a modular suite that offers common services such as authentication and payment collection. Third party developers can also create DIGIT modules, and plenty have done so and now offer add-ons that handle tasks as diverse as managing birth and death certificates, revenue collection, and running water treatment plants. DIGIT is ubiquitous in India, where all state and union territory governments use the platform, as do over 20,000 local government entities. India also exports DIGIT under its policy of turning software created for its own needs into “digital public goods” (DPI) that it happily gives away to other nations. Nine nations have implemented DIGIT to some degree, among them Mozambique, Liberia, Senegal, Nigeria, Burundi, Ethiopia, Indonesia, Jamaica, and Sri Lanka India’s population is 1.4 billion. Indonesia’s is 280 million and Nigeria is home to 240 million. DIGIT is therefore used by governments that serve over two billion people, some of whom are now at risk thanks to CVE-2026-136706 , a 9.3-rated SQL injection flaw present in DIGIT which allows “improper neutralization of user supplied input while constructing SQL queries and execution in the affected User and Access Control Service components.” “An unauthenticated remote attacker could exploit this vulnerability by sending specially crafted input through the affected API endpoint to the targeted system,” according to CERT-IN . “Successful exploitation of this vulnerability could allow the attacker to execute arbitrary SQL queries, potentially resulting in unauthorized disclosure, modification or deletion of database information on the targeted system.” eGov India, which oversees work on DIGIT, has released source code for an update that fixes the problem. While local government users of DIGIT typically access it as SaaS, through large implementations run by national or state governments, over 1,000 deployments are live across various cities and other entities. Those orgs can therefore add patching DIGIT to their urgent to-do lists, along with fixing Java , PHP , vCenter and any other widely used technologies that suddenly need an urgent security update. ®

technology.title: The token factory never sleeps
technology.description: Agentic AI has supercharged demand for inference infrastructure. According to Goldman Sachs, token consumption is set to jump 24-fold to 120 quadrillion tokens per month between this year and 2030. Enterprises, wary of frontier model sticker shock, are now building their own GPU estates to cope. Those enterprises shouldn't blindly follow hyperscalers' lead when taking AI inference kit into production. The indicators of success for such companies are different than those for a frontier model provider, and so are the constraints. DIY AI infrastructure at the enterprise level has to earn ROI quickly, meaning that enterprises must focus on sustained operation. That makes engineering criteria such as uptime, heat and power, service windows, and deployment times doubly important. The performance benchmarks that hyperscalers focus on won't matter nearly as much to the average bank or retailer. ASUS is presenting the ASUS NVIDIA HGX Rubin System , built on the NVIDIA HGX Rubin NVL8 platform, as a worked example of sustained AI inference infrastructure. It announced two models at NVIDIA GTC Berlin in October: the 3U hybrid-cooled XR R1I12B-M1BHFS and the 2U fully liquid-cooled XR R1I12B-M1BLFS . Agents change the compute bill Agents represent a hockey stick curve for token consumption because an agent isn't a single prompt. It loops until the job's done, often spawning other versions of itself in the process. This is how it breaks a goal into steps and works through them iteratively. While training is a batch workload, agent inference is a production service that runs around the clock and only gets bigger. NVIDIA is making each generation of systems more powerful than the last to keep up with the demands of both. Running at scale, day after day, is another matter. A useful way to think about the infrastructure that does it is as a token factory: it takes in power, data and GPU compute and turns out tokens. What counts is throughput, meaning how many tokens, and how many users, the same power and floor space can serve, hour after hour. Enterprises move from pilots to AI factories Enterprises are moving ahead quickly with their AI factory projects. According to Deloitte's AI infrastructure survey , published in March, 64 percent of respondents have started limited or at-scale AI factory deployments, while 88 percent expect to do so by 2028. They are spending more on AI infrastructure to do it: 86 percent expect their budgets to increase over the next three years. Enterprises have different problems from hyperscalers and frontier model companies, though. Model builders often get to design greenfield campuses around their GPUs. Conversely, enterprises are often working with small operations teams in existing datacenters that may not have been built with AI in mind. technology.title: Microsoft: Hackers in China, N Korea using ARTEX AI tool to break into global tech systems
technology.description: Chinese and North Korean state-sponsored hacking crews are among the growing number of groups known for using the ARTEX pentesting tool in attacks, Microsoft said this week. ARTEX is an open source, AI-powered penetration testing framework that attackers have adopted to automate reconnaissance, credential attacks, and exploitation since its public release in July. Campaigns that have been linked to ARTEX have targeted cloud environments, IT software like ConnectWise , and financial institutions globally, sometimes reaching privileged access in under three hours. Salt Typhoon is arguably the most recognizable name on the list of ARTEX beneficiaries – the group responsible for attacks on telcos AT&T and Verizon , US government systems , UK prime minister's aides , and more. The lesser-known Crystal Typhoon – the group behind the ArcaneDoor attacks back when Microsoft called it Storm-1849 – was also named alongside it, as were North Korea's Onyx Sleet and Pearl Sleet. Microsoft also named China-state-aligned Storm-0940, linked to the ConnectWise compromise, and financially motivated, Cambodia-based Storm-3358. It had previously reported both groups' use of ARTEX. Chinese cybersecurity company ThreatBook claimed ownership of ARTEX in November. GitHub user "Autumn-27" originally published its source code with a Chinese-language interface in July. Various forks of the repo, which was taken down in October, have meant that the same framework is available in multiple languages. According to Infrawatch , there are more than 130 variants of ARTEX in circulation, and it is the most widely used agentic offensive framework (AOF) at present. Like other offensive security tools adopted by criminals, ARTEX can lower the effort required to mount attacks. Experienced groups can also use it to automate repetitive work and pursue multiple avenues at once. As Microsoft echoed this week, after the FBI and AWS issued their warnings earlier this month , ARTEX is proving to be a useful tool for the more sophisticated groups to streamline and hasten their attacks too. It's being used to help attackers steal AI and cloud credentials at "industrial scale," as AWS put it, which provide attackers access to advanced models for free. Microsoft says ARTEX can progress from reconnaissance to persistent, privileged access within minutes, depending on its configuration and the target's defenses. "In the past few weeks, we've reported several distinct campaigns that abused ARTEX to search public repositories for exposed secrets, enable supply chain compromise, and scan internet-facing systems for exploitation," its threat intelligence team blogged . technology.title: The Garmin Forerunner 265S is down to $300, its best price of the year
technology.description: The Forerunner 265S is great for runners with small wrists. | Photo by Amelia Holowaty Krales / The Verge The Forerunner 265S may not be the newest or flashiest Garmin, but it’s one that I’ve always loved most in testing. For runners with smaller wrists, it fits nicely. The battery life is pretty good thanks in part to its OLED touchscreen. When I reviewed it a few years ago, I called it the Goldilocks of fitness watches at the time, and the only thing that bugged me was its price. But now that it’s down to $299.99 (a $150 discount off its MSRP) at Amazon and Best Buy for Black Friday, I can easily recommend it. Garmin Forerunner 265S (42mm) Garmin’s Forerunner 265S is identical to the standard 265, only it features a slightly better battery life and a smaller 42mm build for those with more petite wrists. Where to Buy: $449.99 $299.99 at Amazon $449.99 $299.99 at Best Buy The neat thing about Garmins in general is that you really don’t need the latest models to get the most out of the company’s platform. Its watches tend to get firmware updates for several years after launch, which is how long the average Garmin user tends to hold on to theirs. This particular watch is best suited for folks who want something a bit slimmer and smaller, enjoy a pop of color, and want a little extra fitness tracking prowess — but don’t need the whole kit and caboodle that sends the price up by hundreds. There are a few other Garmin models I like that are also on sale during Black Friday. I wish that I had 10 arms to fully vet every single last one, but alas. Garmin’s Venu 4 is $449 at Amazon , Best Buy , and REI , an 18 percent discount. This is a great option if you’re looking for more of a smartwatch that does fitness than a fitness-y watch that looks like a smartwatch. It’s a fine line, but if you know, you know. Finally, Garmin’s Forerunner 970 is $100 off, costing $649 at Amazon , Best Buy , and REI . This is what I’d recommend to marathoners who need something a bit more robust but not as heavy-duty as the flagship Fenix line. I’ve used it to train for a few races and it’s a solid upper-midrange (for Garmin!) option.

technology.title: Tech's outage problem needs maintenance, not conspiracy theories
technology.description: Years of technical debt, increasingly complex systems, and underinvestment in IT operations have left organizations vulnerable to major outages, according to Forrester. The analyst pointed to a seven-day stretch in November when failures disrupted Microsoft 365, US air traffic control, banking, and other critical services. The coinciding outages provoked "a slew of conspiracy theories about cyberattacks and AI," Forrester said. "The real culprit is tragically mundane: the culmination of decades of technical debt, the frenetic buildout of massively complex and highly interdependent systems, the concentration of risk, and the underinvestment in advanced operations." Forrester urged technology suppliers and in-house IT teams to prioritize resilience as their systems grow more complex. Otherwise, "the tech estate will collapse like a house of cards, taking down consumer and business trust with it." Earlier this month, Microsoft was left struggling to restore many of its cloud services after a core process running on some servers became "overwhelmed" and its attempts to fix the problem failed. Some of its services did not recover for another 24 hours. In October, Google Cloud blamed a "power event" for taking down multiple online products for customers in Western Europe. Affected services included BigQuery Data Transfer Service, Cloud Filestore, Cloud Run, Google App Engine, and Google Kubernetes Engine. In October last year , a major outage impacted Amazon Web Services (AWS), with even Amazon's own web page reported to be offline and dozens of other online services and websites affected. Aviation and banking were also hit this month. A communications outage triggered a nationwide ground stop in the US on November 13 , while incidents involving JPMorgan Chase, United Airlines, Apple, Workday, Gmail, and other services added to the sense of widespread instability. "Claims that these were all part of one connected cyberattack or conspiracy are highly unlikely. The real story is much more mundane," the report said . Forrester argued that organizations have prioritized visible improvements over repairs to the underlying technology. "Modernization investments have favored visible change over structural renewal," wrote report authors Lauren Nelson and Mark Moccia. "Organizations routinely fund new customer experiences, cloud migrations, platform consolidation, and AI initiatives because leaders can connect them to growth or productivity. "They are less enthusiastic about updating core systems, simplifying architectures, retiring obsolete components, and eliminating fragile interfaces. The result is a modern front end resting on an aging, brittle, and increasingly interconnected estate." Forrester's recommendations are to map dependencies, test failures and recovery under realistic conditions, and use incidents and near misses to identify weaknesses before they cause another outage. ®
